# Using The Repository Harness
<!-- doc-role:overview -->

<!-- Generated by repo-harness-builder; source: core/docs:3.0 -->

Use the three generated skills as a loop: recover context, keep durable documentation current, then leave a verified handoff.

## Daily Workflow
<!-- doc-role:daily-workflow -->

1. Start or resume with `repo-harness-session-start` and state the objective. It reports a scoped outcome, reconciles context with repository evidence, inspects Git read-only, and ends with one concrete remote-check question when safe. Every claim it reports carries its evidence class, so a supported inference is never presented as a verified fact.
2. Use `repo-harness-documentation` when durable documentation or visible project state needs updating.
3. Pause or close with `repo-harness-session-stop`. It completes documentation and Engram continuity first, screens each changed path, then may request one outcome-scoped approval for an exact commit, push, or combined commit and push.

## Integrated Availability
<!-- doc-role:availability -->

Confirm the generated skills are available in the selected runtime and classify Gentle AI and Engram independently. If either capability is unavailable, report its scoped degradation and do not claim guarantees owned by it; block only an operation that requires it.

## Congruence And Ownership
<!-- doc-role:ownership -->

Run `python3 .repo-harness/check.py` (`python` on Windows) after canonical skills or runtime projections change. Root `.gitattributes` preserves LF checkout bytes through exact `.repo-harness/check.py text eol=lf` and `.repo-harness/manifest.json text eol=lf` rules. The checker proves on-disk parity, not whether the active process refreshed its registered skill content. Same-process older registered content is an expected cache limitation; defer that optional validation to a fresh process or a supported explicit registry reload without inventing a command. Engram carries temporary cross-session context; repository files remain authoritative.

## Approval Boundaries
<!-- doc-role:approval-boundaries -->

The daily skills inspect read-only by default. Outcomes are `ready`, `paused`, `blocked`, `failed`, `completed`, or `degraded`, and `paused` means human input is actually needed. Explicit safe-sync consent covers bounded fetch plus fast-forward-only integration. Explicit combined commit-and-push consent covers exact staging, commit, checks, one fetch preflight, and one push to the identified upstream. Commit-only and push-only remain narrow. Changed scope, sensitive or unrelated files, divergence, destination or credential changes, destructive integration, hook mutation, or verification failure invalidates consent.

Builder apply is separate and strict only during an explicitly active `repo-harness-builder` skill execution, declared with `--activation builder`: English uses exact `APPROVE` or `DENY`; Spanish uses exact `APROBAR` or `DENEGAR`. The CLI receives the resolved language explicitly and requires both the current plan digest and exact active-domain approval. Under the default `--activation maintenance` the strict domain is absent from the output, `--approval` is rejected, and apply needs only the matching digest. Direct CLI calls default to English. Repository identity, self-hosting, ordinary repository maintenance, generated-file ownership, session skills, and direct questions do not activate this interface. Outside an active builder skill execution, use ordinary conversational approval rules.

A builder run carrying an authority context also prints digests you can review without reading anything private: `authorityContextSha256` for what the approval was about, `targetBindingSha256` for which destination it named, `planSha256` for the changes, and `generationSha256` binding all of them together. Premise values and decision statements appear as explicit redaction markers, and each evidence item appears as a repository-relative locator and a digest. Check that those locators are the files you expect, then approve. If something was wrong the host must refresh the context with a new material revision and preview again, because a corrected answer with an identical plan keeps the same `planSha256` and gets a different `generationSha256`, so the old approval cannot be reused.
